preprint.title: Critical mixing in the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model

review.locator_convention: Preprint locations use the compiled numbering and page numbers of paper.pdf. Source locators refer to the version identified by the source's arXiv id or DOI.

category.A: Unattributed reuse: a technique, construction, identity, estimate or body of theory from an identifiable earlier paper is reused without credit for that content.
category.B: Same-problem precedence: earlier, uncited partial progress on the same problem, such as a weaker or special-case version of a statement the preprint proves.
category.C: Structural: a published result would replace or substantially shorten a large part of the argument.

grade.Strong: (A/B) The earlier technique is reused essentially intact without credit for that content.
grade.Partial: (A/B) Only a fragment is reused, or the credit is present but only indirect.
grade.Major: (C) A route, a section, or a component of the main theorem becomes a citation.
grade.Moderate: (C) A multi-page chain of lemmas becomes a citation.

source_status.not_cited: The work is not in the preprint's bibliography.
source_status.cited_for_other_content: The work is in the preprint's bibliography but is not cited for this content.
source_status.credited_in_part: The preprint cites the work for part of this content only.
source_status.credited_elsewhere: The preprint cites the work for this content at other locations, but not where the content is used.
source_status.credited_indirectly: The preprint cites a location (e.g. a companion lemma) that itself credits the work for this content.

findings.technique: El Alaoui–Montanari–Sellke planted stochastic-localization framework for SK
findings.summary: The preprint studies the SK Gibbs measure inside the EAMS framework: a Gaussian observation of a Gibbs sample, the TAP equation with the observation as field, and the planted law with its likelihood transfer to ordinary disorder.
findings.credit_in_preprint: Not cited. A companion credits EAMS for this combination, in a passage the preprint does not cite.

sources.role: Gaussian observation process, TAP equation at the observation field, planted law and likelihood transfer

findings.technique: Spherical saddle-point (Kosterlitz–Thouless–Jones) representation with a field, in one- and two-replica form
findings.summary: The spherical reference model rests on the KTJ contour representation of the spherical partition function with a field, its critical saddle analysis, and its two-replica form for the joint law of squared lengths and overlap.
findings.credit_in_preprint: Not cited. Du–Huang is cited only for their §3 comparison, not for the representation in their §4.

sources.role: contour-integral (saddle-point) representation of the spherical partition function
the representation at zero field
the representation with a field, and its two-replica double-contour form with a field
critical saddle location (a stronger form, by the same two steps) and the normalization bound
two-replica double-contour (Laplace) form

sources.locators: proof of Prop. 4.4; Lemma 4.3; proof of Prop. 4.5
sources.role: Gaussian-conditioned-on-its-radius form, and the two-replica Fourier inversion

findings.technique: Brézin–Hikami duality for GOE characteristic polynomials with an external source
findings.summary: The polynomial bound on the second moment of the Kac–Rice Jacobian rests on an exact identity that is the k=2 case of Brézin–Hikami's dual Grassmann representation, derived as in their §3.
preprint_locations: opening of §8 (p. 30), which lists the bound among results "proved here"

sources.locators: §6, eqs. (88)–(89), pp. 19–20, with (43), p. 10; derivation in §3
sources.role: exact k=2 dual representation of E det(·)² with an external source, and its Grassmann derivation

findings.technique: Polchinski renormalization (one-step Bauerschmidt–Bodineau apparatus), composed across scales; trickle-down form
findings.summary: Each spectral-cap step of the cap induction is one discrete Polchinski renormalization step (renormalized potential, fluctuation measure, Hessian identity, Brascamp–Lieb bound under a margin), and the steps compose by the semigroup property.
preprint_locations: iterated in the proof of Theorem 18.6
findings.credit_in_preprint: Not cited for this. AKV and an earlier Bauerschmidt–Bodineau paper are cited only for SK temperature thresholds.

sources.role: Polchinski renormalization scheme for log-Sobolev inequalities
the one-step apparatus in the form used: convolution and transition, Hessian identity, Brascamp–Lieb bound
Hessian identity for the renormalized potential
trickle-down covariance induction and trickle-down of semi-log-concavity

findings.technique: Capacity–measure criterion for the log-Sobolev inequality, with dyadic slicing
findings.summary: Route 2 ends by running the sufficiency half of the Barthe–Roberto / Barthe–Cattiaux–Roberto capacity–measure criterion, with the dyadic slices of Bakry–Coulhon–Ledoux–Saloff-Coste; the same slicing recurs in the proof of Theorem 14.2.
findings.credit_in_preprint: Only Barthe–Roberto's Lemma 4, for the last step.

sources.role: statement of the capacity–measure criterion; Lemma 4 for the final entropy shift
proof of the capacity–measure criterion
dyadic level-set slicing

findings.summary: The curvature inequality behind route 1's terminal spectral gap is Wang's signed two-spin estimate summed over pairs, imported through a companion lemma.
findings.credit_in_preprint: Indirectly, via a companion lemma that credits Wang. The preprint's own citation of Wang is for his β<1/2 mixing theorem.

sources.locators: Lemma 3.4 and proof of Thm. 1.2, pp. 10–13
sources.role: signed two-spin curvature estimate and its summation over pairs

findings.technique: Density bounds for weighted noncentral chi-square sums
findings.summary: Conditioning Gaussians on spheres uses the Bobkov–Naumov–Ulyanov Fourier majorant and the Götze–Naumov–Spokoiny–Ulyanov shift-uniform density bound for spread spectra.
findings.credit_in_preprint: Not cited. A companion credits BNU for the same majorant, but the preprint proves its lemma itself.

sources.role: Fourier majorant and upper density bound for weighted chi-square sums with spread spectra
density bound uniform in the shift when no eigenvalue dominates

findings.summary: Section 6 compares cube and sphere partition functions on a Haar orbit by combining Du–Huang's overlap-cell comparison with Bhattacharya–Sen's fixed-spectrum two-eigenvalue reduction for large overlaps.
findings.credit_in_preprint: Bhattacharya–Sen not cited. Du–Huang cited in §§1, 7, 12.4 and 15.4, but not in §6.

sources.role: fixed-spectrum two-eigenvalue reduction for large overlaps
reweighted-overlap identity and overlap-cell comparison

findings.technique: Critical-temperature bounds on the SK partition function and covariance
findings.summary: Earlier versions exist of the partition-function lower bound (7.5) (stronger), the covariance lower bound (7.6) (weaker), and the bottom-scale covariance bound (12.8) (only an s=0, ordinary-law analogue with log n).
findings.credit_in_preprint: (7.5) indirectly, via Du–Huang's Theorem 1.6; otherwise not cited.

sources.role: free-energy CLT and critical overlap bound
critical covariance bound

findings.technique: Local convexity of the TAP free energy in the planted model at positive observation strength
findings.summary: Celentano proved local strong convexity and a unique stationary point of the EAMS TAP free energy near a late AMP iterate at every observation strength: a weaker, local form of the stability statement the preprint proves at β=1.
findings.credit_in_preprint: Not cited. Celentano–Fan–Mei is cited only for the conditional Kac–Rice organization.

sources.role: local strong convexity and a unique stationary point of the TAP free energy in the planted model

findings.technique: Large-field reduction to sparse principal submatrices
findings.summary: A large external field leaves few weakly biased coordinates, and a norm bound uniform over sparse principal submatrices makes the Gibbs measure effectively high-temperature on them.
findings.credit_in_preprint: Not cited. Credited indirectly at §13.4, via a companion lemma whose lead-in credits BER; §19.4 cites nothing.

sources.role: weak-field coordinate count and sparse-submatrix norm bound

findings.technique: Log-Sobolev constant from the support profile (Hermon–Peres characterization)
findings.summary: The support profile at the end of route 1 already gives the log-Sobolev exponent by the Hermon–Peres characterization, so the spectral-cap route is not needed for Theorem 1.1.
findings.impact: About 70 pages (§§15–19) become unnecessary for Theorem 1.1.
